records.name: Arte Museum
records.address: ICON Park, 8375 International Dr, Orlando, FL
records.description: Mark the calendar for 2027, when Arte Museum is set to arrive at ICON Park. The immersive digital art experience comes from Korean design powerhouse d'strict, whose locations in Las Vegas, New York, Dubai and Seoul have drawn large crowds. Galleries promise towering waterfalls, glowing floral fields, tranquil forests and aurora skies, brought alive with projection mapping, enveloping soundscapes and custom scents. Every room invites you to step inside the art, not just look at it. Orlando's version gets all-new works made for Central Florida, which makes it one to watch.

holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class A: the description says arrival in 2027; the record's own opening_soon field reads Late 2027.

records.name: Category 10
records.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
records.description: Luke Combs is bringing a hurricane to CityWalk, in name at least. Category 10, named for his hit "Hurricane," is set to open in late 2027 as a 33,000-square-foot, three-story country music venue at Universal Orlando. Plans call for live country music, free line dancing, Carolina-style food honoring Combs' North Carolina roots and experiential spaces inspired by his songs. It would be the third location after Nashville and Las Vegas, and the first built with a theme-park crowd in mind. Country fans should watch this one.

holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class A: Luke Combs venue at Universal CityWalk, set to open in late 2027.

records.name: Tropical Americas
records.address: Disney's Animal Kingdom, 2901 Osceola Pkwy, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
records.description: DinoLand is gone, and an 11 acre village is rising in its place. Tropical Americas, opening in fall 2027, recreates northern South America and Central America in Pueblo Esperanza, the Village of Hope. Announced headliners include an Indiana Jones expedition into a Mayan temple and Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto, the first Encanto ride, set inside the Casita on the day Antonio receives his gift. A hand carved animal carousel and a large quick service hacienda round out the land.

holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class A: opening in fall 2027; the land replacing DinoLand is still rising.

records.name: Disney Lakeshore Lodge
records.address: Near Disney's Fort Wilderness Resort, Orlando, FL
records.description: Disney's newest resort opens July 1, 2027, on the shores of Bay Lake between Wilderness Lodge and Fort Wilderness, and it's built around the nature Disney animators have loved for decades. Nine hundred-plus rooms and freestanding Lake Houses draw from Bambi, Pocahontas, Brother Bear, Encanto, and Fantasia. The lobby centers on floor-to-ceiling lake views, a glowing fiber-optic river, and a blown-glass canopy of hundreds of leaves. A lazy river, multiple pools, water-taxi access to Magic Kingdom, and lounges positioned for fireworks views. The tranquil base camp for your park days.

holdout_note.reason: pre-opening; also no public street address
holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Classes A and B: the description states it opens July 1, 2027; the address is an area phrase, not a street address.

records.name: Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift
records.address: Universal Studios Florida, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL
records.description: New steel is already climbing at Universal Studios Florida. Fast and Furious: Hollywood Drift arrives in 2027, replacing the retired Rip Ride Rockit with outdoor coaster cars that rotate a full 360 degrees to simulate drifting, plus a 170 foot vertical spike that launches riders nearly seventeen stories over the edge of CityWalk. The much criticized Supercharged closed in 2026 to clear the way. Universal is betting the franchise on pure, high speed, sideways throwing thrills, and coaster fans are the clear audience.

holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class A: arrives in 2027, replacing Rip Ride Rockit.

records.name: SEAQuest: Legends of the Deep
records.address: SeaWorld Orlando, 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
records.description: A family ride that keeps everyone together, even when afternoon storms arrive. SEAQuest: Legends of the Deep opens in spring 2026 at SeaWorld as the park's first suspended dark ride. Riders travel through an underwater legend in a new expanded area of the park. Because the experience is weatherproof and family friendly, it fills a real gap in a lineup better known for coasters and animal presentations. Check SeaWorld's site for the exact opening date before you plan a day around it.

holdout_note.expected_opening: Unconfirmed. Copy said spring 2026 but the ride was not open as of 2026-10-13; one report says delayed for redesign with no confirmed date, and one lower-authority post claims Oct 16, 2026.
holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class A, status checked 2026-10-13.

records.name: Pomelo
records.address: 1632 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
records.description: Every Orlando food person has been watching this Mills 50 project. Hung Huynh, the Saigon-born chef who won Top Chef season three and cooked at Per Se and Guy Savoy, is building his first full-scale Orlando restaurant here: a live-fire Southeast Asian room called Pomelo. Expect grilled seafood, skewers and charred octopus, plus a cocktail program built around the pomelo fruit, lemongrass and regional herbs. He describes it as chill, fun and loud, and funky if the durian shows up. Watch for the opening date; this one will draw a crowd.

holdout_note.expected_opening: Announced Nov 2025 for spring 2026; no source found confirming it actually opened.
holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class A (announcements via Orlando Shine and WhatNow); treated as a suspected pre-opening until verified.

records.name: Ramen-Making Class
records.address: Orlando, FL (address confirmed at booking)
records.description: Steam clouds the pot, noodles cook for less time than you expect, and the broth you seasoned starts tasting like a real bowl. A local chef leads this hands-on class from scratch, covering broth and noodles step by step. You work standing up, taste as you go, and finish with the bowl you built yourself. For anyone who orders ramen often, the class changes how you judge the next bowl you meet.

holdout_note.expected_opening: Not applicable; the address is confirmed at booking only.
holdout_note.source: policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md Class B: the address reads Orlando, FL (address confirmed at booking).

records.name: Center Lake Park
records.address: 299 Center Lake Ln, Oviedo, FL 32765
records.description: Oviedo built its new downtown around this lake, and the park is where the whole project proves itself. Center Lake Park wraps the water in three broad lawns, an amphitheatre and cultural center on one shore, and the kind of extras families plan around: a splash pad, a playground, a dog park, and a Veterans Tribute by the water. The cantina keeps the lawn supplied during concerts and movie nights, and the surrounding blocks of Oviedo on the Park put dinner within a short walk. Bring a blanket and let the lake set the pace.

holdout_note.reason: area label held out per owner ruling; a rename to Center Lake Park was ordered and then superseded by this hold-out
holdout_note.source: Owner ruling 2026-10-13; policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md, the Oviedo pattern.

records.name: Park Avenue Historic District
records.address: Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
records.description: The postcard Orlando never sends runs through Winter Park under a canopy of old oaks. Park Avenue is a brick-lined avenue where shopfronts have stood since the twenties, and it made the National Register of Historic Places for good reason: every block feels like a small southern city that refused to be paved over. Stroll it slowly, peek down the side alleys and let a boutique you never planned to enter steal an hour. Locals measure other Orlando streets against this one, which makes it the stroll to prioritize.

holdout_note.reason: area label held out per owner ruling (the Oviedo twin)
holdout_note.source: Owner ruling 2026-10-13; policy-sweep-2026-10-13.md, the Oviedo pattern generalized.

records.name: 600 Block
records.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
records.description: Most people walk straight past it inside Pat O'Brien's, and that is the point. 600 Block is CityWalk's password door speakeasy for guests 21 and up, tucked behind dueling piano noise into a smokier, slower room. A jazz musician sets the tempo, cocktails get careful treatment, and seating outside keeps the piano and CityWalk people watching in earshot. Inside gives you the fuller hushed spell. The room keeps vanishing and returning, so when the door is open, take the chance.

holdout_note.expected_opening: Not applicable. The limited run ended August 23, 2026.

records.name: Zukku-San Sushi Bar & Grill
records.address: Pointe Orlando, 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
records.description: Tampa born Zukku-San opened at Pointe Orlando in April 2026, bringing polished sushi and robata cooking to International Drive. The restaurant, from the Majestic Restaurant Group, centers its draw on the sushi program, while grilled skewers and small plates give non sushi eaters real options at the same table. That balance matters for mixed groups heading to the Pointe theaters or I-Drive nightlife nearby. Choose it for a pre show dinner that feels composed without narrowing the menu to raw fish alone.

holdout_note.expected_opening: Unconfirmed. Announced for March 2026, then April 2026; neither opening happened. Restore when the venue actually opens.

records.address: 5472 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
records.description: A boba craving on the tourist corridor deserves a straightforward fix, not a detour. Boba Club on International Drive serves milk teas, fruit teas, boba shakes, and ice cream fast, in the thick of the I-Drive action. Prices keep a family outing painless, and the menu stays focused on the drinks and scoops you came for. The shop is dedicated to bubble tea rather than treating it as a side item. Choose Boba Club when you want a quick, affordable boba stop that fits the day without reshaping your plans.

records.name: Tierra
records.address: Tierra, 4963 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814
records.description: Baldwin Park has quietly become a serious corridor for Japanese cooking, and Tierra adds another reason to visit. The Baldwin Park room shows the clean lines and calm focus of a proper Japanese kitchen: precise knife work, rice that matters, and fish treated with reverence. Its category promises Spanish Japanese fusion, even as the kitchen reads focused and Japanese in spirit. An evening stroll around Lake Baldwin pairs naturally with dinner here. Let the omakase instinct take over, trust the chef, and keep the night unhurried.

records.name: Diadem Pickleball Complex
records.address: 14748 W Colonial Dr, Winter Garden, FL
records.description: Pickleball's boom gets its Winter Garden cathedral here. Diadem Pickleball Complex is converting a 35,000-plus-square-foot industrial building on West Colonial into an indoor pickleball destination: polished courts, expert coaching, leagues, weekend intro clinics for newcomers, and DUPR-rated tournaments with real prize money. Whether you're learning your first dink or chasing cash in Moneyball divisions, the facility is built for every level. Refuel between matches with food and drinks on site. This is where west Orange County's fastest-growing sport lives.

holdout_note.expected_opening: Unconfirmed. One source expects 2027; a pickleball industry interview said Winter Garden in 2026; no opening evidence exists. Restore when the facility opens.

records.name: Museum of Ice Cream
records.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
records.description: The pinkest thing to ever hit International Drive is planned for Pointe Orlando. The Museum of Ice Cream concept is a multi-sensory playground where unlimited ice cream meets photo-ready rooms, from the iconic sprinkle pool to ice-cream history exhibits, carnival games, a giant slide and a diner pouring cocktails for the grown-ups. Since its 2016 New York pop-up days it has been a sugar rush of interactive rooms, and Orlando is a natural home for it. Check opening status before you roll up with the kids, because timing matters here.

holdout_note.expected_opening: 2026 (coverage says coming in 2026; no date announced)

records.name: Society Park
records.address: 8001 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
records.description: A country club idea gets traded for padel courts, pickleball, and dinner. Society Park, described as a Gen Z country club, is a sports and entertainment complex on International Drive built around active socializing. You get nine padel courts, an exhibition court, children's courts, and three pickleball courts, plus a pro shop, a spa, and two restaurants. Come for a match and stay for dinner if your ideal night out mixes exercise, food, and friends in one address.

holdout_note.source: Audit C-schema-venues.md (2026-10-15): press coverage describes a fall 2026 opening at 8001 International Dr.

records.name: Eola Food Hall
records.address: 150 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL
records.description: Downtown's newest food hall lives in the bones of the old University Club, the 1926 social club that watched a century of Orlando pass. Thirteen vendor stalls fill the lower floor, while a speakeasy and wine bar sit on the second, with events, musicians and DJs in the mix. Croissant Gourmet arrived first, bringing French pastry, five kinds of French toast and nine varieties of crepes to its first Orlando location. Steps from the Lake Eola skyline, it upgrades downtown eating without erasing the building's past.

holdout_note.source: Audit C-schema-venues.md (2026-10-15): press calls it upcoming and the venue's own site copy is future tense; caught by the audit's random sample, not pre-flagged in the dataset.

records.name: Jiang's Kitchen (Mills 50)
records.address: 1111 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
records.description: A noodle shop dreamed up from childhood becomes Mills 50 theater you can eat. Restaurateur Eric Jiang, the chef behind Sushi Izuki omakase, built this Jiang's Kitchen around handcrafted noodles and dumplings. An open kitchen lets you watch noodles stretch and pull while soup dumplings fold by hand nearby. Regional Chinese specialties include biang biang noodles, dan dan noodles, and wontons in chili oil, plus beer, wine, sake, and bubble teas. Across from Mills Market on East Colonial, it suits you when craft and spectacle should arrive in the same bowl.

holdout_note.source: The record's own opening_soon field reads 'Announced'; Audit D-editorial.md section 9 counts it among the four opening-soon records live in the guide.

records.name: Cosa Nostra Italian Deli (Winter Garden)
records.address: 32 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
records.description: The family-run Italian deli that built its name in Clermont is crossing into downtown Winter Garden, taking over the beloved former Writer's Block Bookstore space on Plant Street. Cosa Nostra does made-to-order Italian sandwiches the proper way: the Super Tuscany stacks prosciutto di Parma, salami, mortadella, and fresh mozzarella with pesto and roasted peppers; the Muffaletta Nostra is a tower of Italian meats, cheeses, and giardiniera. Fresh pastas, specialty coffees, and imported Italian groceries round it out. Neighborhood-style hospitality, premium ingredients, zero pretension.

holdout_note.source: The record's own opening_soon field reads 'Announced'; Audit D-editorial.md section 9 counts it among the four opening-soon records live in the guide.

records.name: Oak & Stone
records.address: 310 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
records.description: The fun starts at a tap wall with dozens of craft beers and wines that you pour yourself, at your own pace, tasting as you go. Oak & Stone pairs that playfulness with stone-fired pizzas built on dough made with triple-filtered water and a 36-hour ferment, so the crust has real character under toppings like the buffalo-chicken "winger." The result is a classic American tavern sharpened up: laid-back, buzzing and great for groups. Pour a little, pour a pint; the wall rewards sampling either way.

holdout_note.source: The record's own opening_soon field reads 'Late 2026 / early 2027'; Audit D-editorial.md section 9 counts it among the four opening-soon records live in the guide.

records.name: Nigel's Bananas
records.address: 334 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL
records.description: A chef's dream about his late father, Nigel, turned bananas into a family business. Nigel's Bananas began after that dream suggested bananas would matter, and the result is chocolate-dipped frozen bananas cloaked in Belgian chocolate and loaded with toppings. Toasted coconut and caramel, cookies and cream, and marshmallow drizzle lead the joyful menu. The family-owned Florida treat was born in Seaside and is heading for Park Avenue in Winter Park. Join the line when it opens if playful, handheld dessert sounds like your kind of nostalgia.

holdout_note.source: The record's own opening_soon field reads 'Announced'; Audit D-editorial.md section 9 counts it among the four opening-soon records live in the guide.

records.name: Beginner Sushi-Making Class
records.address: Ten10 Brewing Company, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
records.description: Your first roll leans, your second holds, and someone trades a piece for a sip of beer. A beginner sushi making class at a local brewery teaches rolls step by step in a relaxed setting built for first timers. The pint in front of you and the low stakes keep nerves down while your hands learn the work. Reserve spots together so you share a table, and pick this for a date or friends night where doing something beats just watching.

records.name: Little Sister Dumpling
records.address: 713 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
records.description: Mills 50 gets a dumpling specialist that treats a small format with serious craft. Little Sister Dumpling, the district's new spot on North Mills Avenue, works an Asian fusion kitchen through Korean inflected flavors alongside classic techniques. Everything is hand folded and made to be eaten immediately, which is the point of a dumpling done right. Slide into a seat along Mills and order a spread to share with the table. Choose it when you want to taste why this district keeps turning out focused, confident food stops.

records.name: The Reverie
records.address: 533 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
records.description: The most anticipated opening of Winter Park's year lives in the space Chez Vincent called home for 28 years. At 533 W New England Ave in Hannibal Square, The Reverie is the new American brasserie from two-time James Beard nominee Brandon McGlamery, the chef behind Luma on Park and Prato. The promise is refined yet approachable cooking with French and European roots: classic technique meeting ingredient-driven dishes that stay grounded and craveable, classic cocktails with seasonal twists, and a thoughtful list spanning New and Old World wines. Winter Park is holding its breath.

records.name: La Palette Artisan Ice Pops
records.address: 12720 S Orange Blossom Trl Suite 24, Orlando, FL 32837
records.description: A little paleta shop honors the Latin American popsicle tradition with real fruit. La Palette offers over fifty flavors, with fruit you can taste in chunks: passion fruit, mango, guava, and strawberry. Creamy options get serious too, including Nutella, coconut, and cookie crumble, plus filled paletas hiding condensed milk or dulce de leche at the core. The Oreo version contains a whole Oreo inside, a neat summary of the shop's generosity. Choose a paleta when Florida heat calls for relief that still tastes like fruit.

records.name: Gentry's BBQ
records.address: 1215 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
records.description: Championship technique meets two regional traditions on one Winter Park tray. Pitmaster Chris Gentry built Gentry's on Central Texas brisket technique fused with Eastern North Carolina pulled pork and flavors gathered from travels across the South. His world championship mustard sauce leads a line of rubs and sauces, while Friday spreads bring ribs, sweet heat chicken, smoked potato salad, and honey cornbread to a devoted following. Choose it when you want barbecue treated as a craft, not a shortcut.
